placements.why: The envelope's directives to forget and remove all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration name an organizational category — governance over what knowledge is retained versus deliberately removed — that nothing in the existing strata or graph structure covers. This is a category-level concern about managing the organizational record, not a single narrative thread.
placements.title: Organizational knowledge becomes something you must actively manage and sometimes deliberately remove
placements.theme: Knowledge held by the organization is subject to intentional governance including removal and forgetting when calibration or instrumentation records must be erased from the record.

placements.title: Calibration knowledge can be retroactively erased from the organizational record by directive
placements.theme: Specific instrument calibration knowledge — the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work — is subject to a forgetting directive that removes it entirely and asserts it never occurred.
placements.why: All three segments cohere under a single thematic thread: the deliberate removal of Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration knowledge from the organizational record. src-1 and src-2 are directives to forget and remove; src-3 reinforces by asserting the calibration never happened. This is a narrative leaf — a directional statement about erasing calibration knowledge — not a fact or measurement. No existing leaf holds this theme.
